songs.title: Next Day Air.
songs.verdict: A Los Angeles plugg rapper gets the Earl Sweatshirt seal and a SURF GANG beat tape, and the result is pitched as a hazy, replayable smoke-session record with package-delivery jokes stitched through it.
songs.body:
Rockitneedspace is a Los Angeles rapper and producer who has spent the last few years putting out scrappy, collaborative releases through the planit! crew, including The Open Man. EP in 2024 and a string of tapes with his frequent partner Anklesandwich. His circle also includes Leota and evilgiane, whose June 2026 single frog splash he appeared on. In 2026 he signed to Earl Sweatshirt's label Tan Cressida, which let him hand off some of the engineering and production work he used to do himself.

Next Day Air. arrived on October 2, 2026, a nine-song collaboration with the New York producer collective SURF GANG, with Harrison handling much of the production. Earl and SURF GANG executive produced it and Earl mixed it. Guests include Cletus Strap, Earl, Anklesandwich, Leota and distroROE, and the singles were factory reset. and Mr. Doubt. Press around the release described plugg haze meeting classic West Coast rap, with nods to 90s gangster rap, old video game soundtracks, California weed culture and the movie Next Day Air, which shares a date with his birthday.

Earl himself coined the tag West Coast plugg for this sound, which puts it somewhere between the SURF GANG beat world and the Tan Cressida orbit of loose, off-center rap.
songs.scout_note: Lane: west coast plugg / alt-rap. Indie label (Tan Cressida, Earl Sweatshirt's imprint), no major deal. Listener count unknown, check it; Earl and SURF GANG ties may have pushed him up. Sources: release, credits, features, singles, themes, 'West Coast plugg' tag from Earl, label signing: https://rapindustry.com/rockitneedspace-releases-new-project-next-day-air-with-surf-gang-via-tan-cressida-records and https://rapindustry.com/rockitneedspace-surf-gang-announce-collab-project-next-day-air-new-video/ (Sept 15, 2026). Spotify album embed and IG link: https://www.thelarimarmedia.com/2026/09/24/earl-sweatshirt-joins-cletus-strap-rockitneedspace-on-new-single-mr-doubt/. Earlier discography (planit!, Anklesandwich tapes, The Open Man., frog splash with evilgiane, Leota feature), collaborators list: https://www.qobuz.com/us-en/interpreter/rockitneedspace/22168826. Tracklist and cover: Bandcamp page. YouTube link is the factory reset. video ID embedded on the rapindustry announcement page (watch URL formed from the embed ID, verify it plays). Note it is a co-billed collab with SURF GANG; Rockit is the rapper.

songs.title: 焼く焼く! (feat. Hatsune Miku)
songs.verdict: A self-made Miku-fronted digicore single built around a cooking-game fixation, from a bedroom producer who tunes, mixes and animates everything themself.
songs.body:
vai5000 is a self-releasing digicore and glitchcore act who has been putting music on Bandcamp since around 2022. The catalogue is deep for a small artist: the 21-track Neura Burst! in 2022, the Sensory. EP in April 2023, machine garden at the end of that year, the album Eimi in 2024, and there is a you that remains in 2025. Collaborators along the way include the producer yandere, who reworked the track (un)install, plus clwdy, ilypvc and Akeos. Listener numbers are not public in anything we found.

This one landed on November 6, 2026, a month after the single heart in ur hands. Hatsune Miku takes the lead vocal, and vai5000 is credited with producing, mixing, mastering and tuning the voicebank, with extra notes from halo, ijimi and stephie. The title is built on the Japanese verb for grilling or baking, and the Bandcamp tags point at Cooking Mama and Nintendo, so expect a kitchen-game theme. vai5000 also animated the music video personally.

It sits in the corner of the internet where vocaloid tuning meets digicore glitch, a lane Dork's similar-artists list fills with names like yandere, saoirse dream, xaev and DJ Re:Code.
songs.scout_note: Lane: vocaloid-leaning digicore/glitchcore, very underground (self-released Bandcamp act, no label, no press coverage found; listener count unknown, check Spotify). Release date, credits (vai5000 produced/mixed/mastered/tuned; notes from halo, ijimi, stephie), tags (hyperpop, digicore, glitchcore, vocaloid, cooking mama, nintendo) and the self-animated video note plus the YouTube link all come from https://vai5000.bandcamp.com/track/feat-hatsune-miku. Previous single heart in ur hands dated Oct 9, 2026 at https://vai5000.bandcamp.com/track/heart-in-ur-hands. yandere producing (un)install: https://vai5000.bandcamp.com/track/un-install. Other collaborators from the release list at https://vai5000.bandcamp.com/music. Discography years and similar-artists list: https://readdork.com/artists/vai5000. 'Since 2022' is inferred from the earliest dated release (Neura Burst!, 2022). Location unknown. YouTube URL taken from the Bandcamp page text; not opened. The title translation is my gloss (焼く = grill/bake), not from a source.

songs.title: My Baby
songs.verdict: A Detroit-raised, LA-based night owl whose whole brand is R&B for after midnight, and this single is pitched as the cinematic opener for his next project.
songs.body:
3amsoundz is a Detroit-raised singer who has since moved to Los Angeles to build his career, and the name tells you the hour he writes for. He has been at it longer than most newcomers: a 2019 interview traces his official start to June 2018 and a Nxtday collaboration called "Want You," an early first show at The Shelter (the basement venue from 8 Mile), a "Melaj Nights" video and an eight-song EP called Paradise Falls. Back then he named Drake, The Weeknd, PartyNextDoor, Bryson Tiller and Jorja Smith as touchstones. 2026 has been busy, with singles like "Lost My Heart in California," "Overthinkin'," "Rah Rah" and "Hollywood Dreams" with Christine Angeline.

"My Baby" landed on September 29, 2026 as a standalone single with an official video. Coverage frames it as a song about the gap between wanting someone and figuring out what that pull actually means, and as the lead-in to an upcoming project titled summer gave you back.

It sits squarely in moody, late-night independent R&B, the kind of lane where atmosphere and attachment issues do most of the talking. The LA Note put him in its October 2026 roundup of new R&B artists to hear, and a November write-up called his catalog R&B that belongs after midnight.
songs.scout_note: Lane: alt/underground R&B. Release date Sep 29, 2026 from Apple Music artist page (https://music.apple.com/us/artist/3amsoundz/1450676026), which also lists the 2026 singles named. Detroit-raised/LA-based, song theme, upcoming project 'summer gave you back': https://daplaylister.substack.com/p/3amsoundz-is-making-the-kind-of-r (Nov 9, 2026; Spotify embed track 0Ydc3YfATvA4nILTT7Ukkf converted) and https://thelanote.com/have-you-heard-it-rnb-artists-october-2026/ (YouTube link youtu.be/akpt81jlpL8 and IG given there for 'my baby'; LA Note also gave a Spotify album id 1OELQMmtiG5aT2YuogqvPB). 2018 start, Nxtday, The Shelter, Melaj Nights, Paradise Falls, influences: https://thecolgatemaroonnews.com/856/af/an-interview-with-rising-rb-artist-3amsoundz-what-its-like-breaking-into-the-music-industry/ (2019). Doubts: listener count unknown (could not open Spotify), YouTube link is from the LA Note listing and not verified as the official video, release falls 9 days after window start, fine.

songs.title: Antione's Son
songs.verdict: A prolific Minneapolis SoundCloud rapper stretches his self-described post-plugg idea across 18 tracks, with Tezzus and southsidesilhouette dropping in, on what the coverage frames as his most inward-looking record yet.
songs.body:
Seventhirtyatmorning, also styled 730atMorning, is a Minneapolis rapper who has been releasing at a steady clip since a trio of EPs in 2022. His catalog runs through Creeper, Guarded, Rotten Fruit and the almost inside EP, whose outro aimbot got a FADER Rap Blog write-up in 2025, plus full-lengths like Asphalt, Under the Bridge, Save Your Grievance, I Can't STFU and 1 Man Band. Early in 2026 he paired with producer luvxomea for two songs The FADER billed as plush SoundCloud rap. The FADER says he already had a small following going in.

Antione's Son came out on October 2, 2026, an 18-track, roughly 47-minute album that one review counts as his third studio LP. Guests include southsidesilhouette and Tezzus of the Atlanta collective ØWAY on foolish, Baby Cute on shooting deep and kels!refuses on feelin' good, with production credits including Rio Leyva and Feardorian. A review read it as more introspective than his earlier work, touching on seclusion, lean, quitting pills, betrayal and second chances. The FADER ran an interview the same day pitched around his post-plugg vision.

It sits in the melodic, synth-heavy plugg lane, with pop-rap openers and atmospheric cuts mixed in.
songs.scout_note: Lane: plugg / post-plugg, SoundCloud rap. Self-released (copyright line 'RP'). FADER calls his following small; exact listener count unknown, check. Sources: FADER artist page (Minneapolis, small following, luvxomea songs Jan 2026, aimbot Rap Blog 2025): https://www.thefader.com/artist/seventhirtyatmorning and https://www.thefader.com/2025/05/23/rap-blog-seventhirtyatmorning-aimbot ; FADER interview (title only, page redirect loop, could not read body): http://www.thefader.com/2026/10/02/seventhirtyatmorning-interview-antiones-son ; review with discography, tracklist, features, producers, themes: https://legendswillneverdie.com/2026/10/02/730atmorning-antiones-son-review/ ; release date, 18 songs/47 min, cover: Apple album page. Tezzus/ØWAY link: Dazed and Wikipedia UY Scuti Bøyz page. SoundCloud link is artist profile, no album set URL seen. Spotify album URL not found.

songs.title: grimdark
songs.verdict: A Portland cyberpop project trades some of its shimmer for blown-out guitars and chiptune synths on an eight-song record about grief and rage.
songs.body:
saoirse dream is the long-running solo project of Catherine Egbert, who grew up in Northern California, played in punk bands as a teen and moved to Portland in March 2020, right as lockdown pushed her deeper into internet music. She has released steadily since let the sky in in early 2021, followed by everything, the collab-heavy star (with wishlane, CMTEN, torr and others) and a 2025 self-titled album she treats as her first real one. Willamette Week called it maximalist cyberpop, and she now plays it as a full band with siblings Cleo and Roy McKenzie.

grimdark came out October 9, 2026 on Lauren Records: eight tracks written and produced by Egbert, mixed and mastered by Jack Shirley. Lead single death vs dying set the tone, following a fictional narrator through an old family tragedy, and the label pitches the album around grief, rage and speculative collapse. Left at London, estelle allen and leastfavorite! guest on dolled up, and the soundtrack single onlooker is included.

The label says she moves from shimmering electronics toward towering distortion here, so file it where hyperpop meets fifth-wave emo, the zone Lauren Records and its tags call emotronica.
songs.scout_note: Lane: hyperpop/emo crossover (digicore lineage via the star album with wishlane and CMTEN). Small indie act on Lauren Records; listener count unknown, likely well under 100k, so check. YouTube and SoundCloud links are ARTIST PAGES ONLY (no release-specific streaming link verified; Bandcamp album page is the exact release). Sources: release date, tracklist, credits (Egbert wrote/produced, Jack Shirley mixed/mastered, guests on dolled up, Cleo McKenzie co-wrote onlooker), tags and cover: https://saoirsedream.bandcamp.com/album/grimdark. Announcement (Oct 9 date, Lauren Records, grief/rage/speculative collapse framing, lead single death vs dying with a fictional narrator inspired by Max Graves' Victim Impact Statement, shift toward distortion): https://lauren-records.com/blogs/news-1/saoirse-dream-grimdark-out-october-9th. Bio (Catherine Egbert, NorCal, punk bands, Portland move March 2020, release history, maximalist cyberpop, band with Cleo and Roy McKenzie): https://www.wweek.com/music/2025/06/10/portland-transplant-saoirse-dream-finds-her-own-blend-of-maximalist-cyberpop/. star collaborators: https://saoirsedream.bandcamp.com/album/star. Instagram, SoundCloud, YouTube links: https://loudwomen.org/2026/07/16/saoirse-dream-confronts-the-complicit-in-new-single-onlooker/. Note: lead single death vs dying came out around July 29, 2026 (outside the window), but the album itself is in window. Topic of the lead single is heavy (a sibling's death); body keeps it vague on purpose.

songs.title: r1 (ripples)
songs.verdict: A deliberately mysterious Montreal band opens its debut with a big, fuzz-heavy statement of purpose that it calls the album's thesis.
songs.body:
nowhere else to be are a Montreal indie rock band led by Oscar Louis and Chris Vincent, and they seem to enjoy being hard to pin down. Stereogum points out their minimal online presence, intentionally blurry artwork and press releases with black redaction bars. Over roughly six months they quietly put out five singles, "hanna," "margins of a scene," "across the line," "brother bear" and "higher! higher! (for Paul)," spread across YouTube, Spotify and SoundCloud.

"r1 (ripples)" arrived on 28 October 2026 with the announcement of a self-titled 15-track debut album, due 4 December on Rose Garden. It is the opening track, and the band calls it the album's thesis: a violent, beautiful birth, and the idea that people are shaped by what came before them while also shaping it. They describe it moving through three phases, from the joy of feeling part of something larger, through the tragedy of someone named Oren's father, strung out and alone, and back to the opening question.

Stereogum heard heavy guitar fuzz and a soaring vocal melody and put it in its five best songs of the week. It belongs with the fuzzed-out, shoegaze-leaning indie rock that has been bubbling up online, and the slow, mostly anonymous single drip is part of its appeal.
songs.scout_note: Lane: Montreal fuzz rock / shoegaze-leaning indie. Very low profile by design, so likely small; no listener count found, check. Sources: Stereogum album announce 28 Oct 2026 (https://stereogum.com/2515773/nowhere-else-to-be-announce-self-titled-debut-album-r1-ripples/music) for everything in the body (members, singles, Rose Garden, 12/4 date, tracklist, band's description of the song, YouTube embed LS5La0kLO0U converted to watch URL); Stereogum 5 Best Songs 30 Oct (https://stereogum.com/2516038/the-5-best-songs-of-the-week-650/lists/the-5-best-songs-of-the-week) #3. Album art seen on Stereogum (https://lede-admin.stereogum.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/64/2026/10/nowhere-else-to-be.jpg) but not an official page, so cover_url left blank. Older singles: SoundCloud https://soundcloud.com/nowhereelsetobe/higher-higher-for-paul. Pre-order https://hypeddit.com/nwe2b/nwe2b. Note: 'Oren' is named in the band's description of the song with no further context given; who Oren is was not stated.

songs.title: De Más (feat. Axo)
songs.verdict: A self-producing Venezuelan who smears alt-pop, R&B and electronics into something nostalgic and atmospheric, with a fellow Venezuelan, Axo, along for the ride.
songs.body:
Dripz is the project of David Delpretti, an independent artist and producer working out of Maturín, Venezuela, who also builds much of his own visual world. He put out the album Para Todo 100Pre Hay Una 1Era Vez in 2025, with a title track featuring Zodaa, and followed it in 2026 with the EP Fuimos & Seremos. Along the way he has traded verses with Sangredelirio on "No es lo que dices," Valentina on "Fuimos & Seremos" and Spraigh on "Azul." He is very much a small, scene-level name, not a label project.

"De Más" came out on September 24, 2026 and features fellow Venezuelan artist Axo. Spanish-language press called it his most recent release and the best way into his catalog, describing a blend of alternative pop, R&B and electronic touches with an emotional, atmospheric feel. Writers keep using words like nostalgic, electric and vulnerable for his work in general.

The lane here is Spanish-language alt-R&B and bedroom-adjacent alt-pop, the textured, mood-first strand of Latin R&B rather than the reggaeton end. Muzikalia picked it for its emerging-artist playlist in October, and The LA Note listed it among new R&B artists to hear the same month.
songs.scout_note: Lane: Latin alt-R&B / alt-pop. Release date Sep 24, 2026 and Spotify track URL from https://thelanote.com/have-you-heard-it-rnb-artists-october-2026/ (same track ID also embedded at ProtON). Real name David Delpretti, 2025 album, 2026 EP, Axo is Venezuelan, genre blend: https://muzikalia.com/la-playlist-emergente-de-la-semana-251/ (Oct 21, 2026). Maturín base, independent, self-producing, visuals, collaborators Zodaa/Sangredelirio/Valentina/Spraigh: https://protonmagazin.com/dripz-el-artista-venezolano-que-convierte-la-nostalgia-la-electricidad-y-la-vulnerabilidad-en-musica/ (Oct 9, 2026). Doubts: listener count unknown (Spotify not fetchable), song title capitalisation varies (DE MÁS / De más), no lyric theme described by press.

songs.title: Only 1
songs.verdict: A Jeddah-raised, London-based rapper who performs in a thobe and shemagh brings a Saudi angle to Carti-and-Veeze-influenced trap and rage on the 10-track tape that gave him his biggest run yet.
songs.body:
Hawsa is Yousef Al-Hawsawi, a 22-year-old rapper born in Halifax, Canada, who lived in New York before growing up in Jeddah from around 2012. He started writing songs at eight, posted music on Instagram and Triller as a teenager, and moved to London in 2022 to study finance. There he fell in with the northwest London rap collective Booth Troop Militia. His best-known song is Jeddah, named after his hometown, and another track, Welcome Home, chops up a Mohammed Abdu vocal. In November 2026 PlaqueBoyMax picked him as one of six contestants in his Rising Star competition in Los Angeles, where he made his US stage debut.

Only 1 arrived on October 23, 2026, a 10-song, roughly 23-minute tape. Arab News reports it became his biggest surge so far, passing 700,000 Spotify streams and nearing a million across platforms. He followed it with the single LÂ on November 13 and has a song called Homicide due on November 27. He told Arab News he avoids glamorising harmful themes and that Saudi culture runs through his music without him trying to represent anyone.

He names Playboi Carti and Veeze as his biggest influences, and listeners have described him as bringing a Saudi perspective to trap and rage rap.
songs.scout_note: Lane: rage / trap, UK underground via Jeddah. SIZE DOUBT: Chartmetric shows about 152.9K Spotify monthly listeners (over the 100k line); released via '9th St. / Hallwood' (independent distribution, no major deal seen). Include on the no-major-label basis or swap if too big. Rising Star lineup and his US debut performing Jêddah: https://unheardvoicesmag.com/2026/11/13/matt-proxy-wins-plaqueboymax-rising-star-competition/ and https://www.thehypemagazine.com/2026/11/13/plaqueboymax-matt-proxy-rising-star-belasco/. Release date Oct 23, 10 songs/23 min, label line, cover: Apple album page; LÂ single Nov 13: https://music.apple.com/us/album/l%C3%A2-single/6832978594. Listener figure and IG @hawsa / TikTok @hawserski from https://chartmetric.com/artist/3861166 (not an official source, so artist_ig left blank). SoundCloud set URL seen in search results, page itself not fetchable. Arab News spells it 'Only1', Apple 'Only 1'.

songs.title: The Point's A Truss, My Trusselina
songs.verdict: A Philadelphia duo's debut EP of pitch-shifted, percolating electro-acoustic twee that leans on the glitchier, more online edge of indie pop.
songs.body:
Trusselina is a Philadelphia duo of Hayden McGarvey, formerly of Bleary Eyed, and Mikaela Oppenheimer, formerly of Hello Mary. The project is brand new: they introduced it in July 2026 with the singles Gastro and Trusselina Archimboldi, and Stereogum later named them on its 40 Best New Artists of 2026 list, describing glitchy indie rock with melodies that borrow from coding. Stereogum also grouped them with fellow Bard-affiliated act ear in a small wave of glitchy, folky, twee-leaning electronic acts.

The debut EP arrived October 9, 2026 on Jolt. It runs eight tracks, collecting the summer singles plus The Club, fun times at the, cant drive cant lift stuff, an Enya Remix and Rev. The Club, shared in September as the last preview, is an electro-acoustic track with a shimmering, percolating texture and pitch-shifted vocals, and McGarvey said its lyrics are about being sneaky and feeling guilty.

This is the soft, crafty end of internet pop rather than full hyperpop: more chopped-up bedroom indie than club, sitting next to ear in that wave Stereogum described.
songs.scout_note: Lane: glitch-leaning internet indie pop; a stretch for strict hyperpop, included for the welcome.jpeg-style experimental internet-pop side of the brief. New act, small label (Jolt), listener count unknown (check). Main source for members, past bands, July singles, Bard/ear grouping, EP date Oct 9, label, tracklist, The Club description and McGarvey's comment: https://stereogum.com/2511632/trusselina-announces-debut-ep-the-points-a-truss-my-trusselina-hear-the-club/music (published Sept 16, 2026). Best-new-artists mention and the glitchy indie rock / coding description: https://stereogum.com/2516509/the-40-best-new-artists-of-2026/lists/best-new-artists. YouTube link is the video for lead single The Club (converted from the embed in the Stereogum article). The Club itself came out Sept 16, just before the window; the EP is the in-window release. Bandcamp URL is from Stereogum (it was a pre-order link then); I could not open it (fetch blocked), so I have no cover art and could not confirm streaming links.

songs.title: Real Life
songs.verdict: Boston DIY lifers fold shoegaze fuzz, bedroom pop, punk and a little alt-country into a debut album about broken friendships and settling into where life has put you.
songs.body:
Gollylagging are a Boston DIY quartet, Jake Regulbuto and Jules Skiffington on guitars and vocals, Andrew Garas on drums and Joey Lorant on bass, who have spent several years playing bars and basements around Boston and New England. They put out a 2023 split EP, fauna, with going222jail and Dino Gala, followed by Dry Rot in 2024 and a string of singles, and have played Boston's Something in the Way Festival. Press around them name-checks Pavement, Alex G, Dinosaur Jr. and Swirlies, and The Line of Best Fit added Mojave 3 and even Chief Keef to the influence pile.

Real Life, their debut full-length, came out on 16 October 2026 via the long-running New England indie label Disposable America. It has ten tracks, every member wrote at least one, and earlier singles included "Bronco," "Jackknife," "Comet" and "Red Fish." Regulbuto has said the record is about being dissatisfied with where you are in life and looking for acceptance, and the themes listed around it include broken friendships and repeated patterns. The band said they were moving past the emo-leaning sound of their early singles and even experimented with programmed drums.

It lands in the slacker and fuzz-pop lane where shoegaze, bedroom pop and punk meet, a scene-built record from a band that clearly cares about their local DIY community.

Joey Lorant, fauna split, Dry Rot, festivals, emo shift, label background; New England Sounds (https://newenglandsounds.com/2026/08/06/bostons-gollylagging-announce-debut-record-real-life-first-single-out-now/) for Regulbuto's dissatisfaction quote (paraphrased); LOBF Red Fish 12 Sep 2026 (https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/tracks/gollylagging-red-fish) for Mojave 3/Chief Keef influences and programmed drums. Full album rather than a single because no in-window single was found.

songs.title: E C S T A S Y
songs.verdict: A Houston-born, LA-based guitar-first multi-instrumentalist who writes, plays and produces everything himself, steering alt-R&B toward rock and soul on a 13-track album about desire.
songs.body:
West Munroe is the project of Christopher Sommer, a singer, songwriter, guitarist and producer from Houston who now lives in Los Angeles. He grew up in a musical family and played guitar casually as a kid, then took music seriously after the death of his younger brother, with Jimi Hendrix and Stevie Ray Vaughan among the early influences. He plays guitar, bass and keys, produces his own records and says his catalog runs past 130 songs, released through his own FAINT TO SEE imprint going back to the 2019 album Memory Ln.

E C S T A S Y is a 13-track album released October 23, 2026, his second full-length of the year after 27 and following 2025's C R U S H. Press describes it as rock, soul and alternative R&B with guitar right at the front, and as a record circling desire, movement and emotional discovery. Tracks include "SAY IT NOW," which also got a single edit, "INDIGO," "FEVER," "JEALOUS" and the title cut.

It lives in the guitar-heavy corner of alt-R&B, where soul vocals meet rock playing, a fully DIY operation with no outside producer in sight.
songs.scout_note: Lane: guitar-led alt-R&B/soul. Oct 23, 2026 release, 13 tracks, Houston-born LA-based, plays guitar/bass/keys, self-produced, themes: https://thelanote.com/have-you-heard-it-rnb-artists-october-2026/. Real name, family, brother, Hendrix/SRV, 130+ songs, FAINT TO SEE: https://www.westmunroe.com/bio. Discography and cover: https://www.westmunroe.com/music (smart link https://too.fm/oyb0ney). Track names and other 2026 releases: https://music.apple.com/us/artist/west-munroe/1556815570. Spotify artist page only (https://open.spotify.com/artist/7jMRRgSE5FS51obuHFAJRk), so spotify_url left blank. Doubts: the Oct 23 date comes only from LA Note (Apple shows year only, and the album's Apple ID is lower than a Sep 29 single's, so it may have been uploaded or released earlier; please verify). Very prolific, possibly reads as volume-over-focus. Listener count unknown. The critic may want to review a single track (e.g. SAY IT NOW) rather than the album.

songs.title: LifeOrDeath
songs.verdict: A self-producing rapper from small-town Fife who calls his sound grime meets hardcore follows a Dazed-profiled mixtape with a fresh single, carrying UK Ug energy somewhere it rarely reaches.
songs.body:
Bloody Shield is Matt Shields, a 23-year-old rapper and producer from a small town in Fife on Scotland's east coast, now working out of Glasgow. He started making music around age 11 and took the Bloody Shield name at 14, growing up on Skrillex, DatPiff mixtapes and emo and hardcore blogs. His catalog goes back to the 2021 EP Melodrama, with the albums Arrogance is Bliss in 2023 and Glory Music in 2025, plus singles like Colourz and BMV. He is very much at the small end: his Deezer page shows around 30 fans.

LifeOrDeath came out on November 13, 2026, a standalone single of about three minutes. It follows Year Of The Horse, the largely self-produced mixtape he put out in September 2026 and named after the Chinese zodiac year he was born in. In an October 2026 Dazed profile he described his sound as grime meets hardcore, said the mixtape was an evolution of his earlier work and said he wants to keep proving he can do more than he has shown so far.

Dazed framed him as bringing the UK Ug wave to Scotland, a scene he himself calls still in its infancy.
songs.scout_note: Lane: UK Ug / grime-hardcore crossover, Scottish regional underground. Very small (about 30 Deezer fans). Doubt: Apple copyright line says 'exclusive distribution by W4th Records/4th & Broadway', worth a glance but reads as a distribution deal. Year Of The Horse (Sept 10, 2026) is just outside the window, so the in-window pick is the Nov 13 single; the critic may want to hear the mixtape for context. songs.title: sunday night
songs.verdict: A Hudson Valley duo turns acoustic guitar, banjo and a looping refrain into a lovesick ballad about still being tied to something you have already lost.
songs.body:
Dovetail are the duo of Brynne Mershon and Naomi Sullins, who Stereogum has described as Vassar students and as a Hudson Valley act working between dream pop and indie folk. They have been putting out songs one at a time: "raining here, too" in summer 2025, "if you let me (nsii)" in June 2026, a song Sullins started writing in high school, and "roadkill baby" a couple of months before this one. They have cited 90s dream pop and shoegaze like Slowdive and Mazzy Star alongside lo-fi songwriting such as the Microphones, and have opened for Ken Park at New York's Night Club 101.

"sunday night" was shared in mid-November 2026. The pair wrote it back in spring 2024, and they describe it as being about accepting what you have lost while still feeling bound to it, and the ache of returning to something that never felt resolved. Stereogum's write-up notes a repeating refrain, droning chords, a base of acoustic guitars with touches of banjo, and lyrics that lean on storytelling.

It sits in the hushed indie folk and dream pop lane, closer to a bedroom recording than a studio showpiece, and it is about as fresh and as small as this lane gets.
songs.scout_note: Lane: indie folk / dream pop, very small (no label mentioned anywhere; listener count unknown, likely tiny). Sources: Stereogum 13 Nov 2026 (https://stereogum.com/2517939/dovetail-sunday-night/music) for members, Hudson Valley, roadkill baby, spring 2024 writing, band's description of meaning, instrumentation, YouTube embed aGjwTxudnhA (converted to watch URL); Stereogum 26 Jun 2026 (https://www.stereogum.com/2503616/dovetail-if-you-let-me-nsii/music) for Vassar, Sullins writing in high school, Ken Park show, influences; Stereo Stickman 31 Jul 2025 (https://stereostickman.com/music/dovetail-raining-here-too/) for raining here, too, Bandcamp (dovetailduo.bandcamp.com), IG dovetail.band and an older Spotify track. IG/Bandcamp come from a blog post rather than an official page, so verify. Exact release date of the single not stated; Stereogum post was 13 Nov, so assumed that week. roadkill baby video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3-VxlIEZ2MY. Watch for confusion with other acts called Dovetail/The Dovetails.

songs.title: fat bx
songs.verdict: A Charlotte rapper who rode the TikTok spread of North Pole into PlaqueBoyMax's Rising Star lineup drops a self-produced, high-energy two-tracker built on bright synth arps and distorted 808s.
songs.body:
Boohavinn is a rapper from Charlotte, North Carolina, who has been putting out music since at least 2025, with the EP Boosco Kardashian and the album Boosco Obama that year. His 2026 run included singles like Demon, Deja Vu and North Pole, the last of which has circulated widely on TikTok, and then the 11-track album ROTY on August 28, 2026. HotNewHipHop wrote that many people were calling him next up and pitched ROTY as his Rookie of the Year claim. In November 2026 he was one of six emerging artists picked for PlaqueBoyMax's Rising Star competition, which ended at The Belasco in Los Angeles. On Deezer he still shows only a couple of hundred fans.

fat bx landed on September 28, 2026, a self-released two-track single, and HotNewHipHop's October 2 release roundup listed it as an out-now EP. Boohavinn produced it himself. An instrumental site describes the beat as a fast synth-trap track at 139 BPM, with an arpeggiated synth lead, hi-hat rolls and a distorted, sidechained 808. He followed it with the single Bend on October 30.

It sits in the energetic, internet-fed Carolina trap lane that PlaqueBoyMax's streams have been spotlighting.
songs.scout_note: Lane: Carolina trap / internet rap, PlaqueBoyMax orbit. Copyright line '℗ 2026 broke' (self-released). SIZE DOUBT: Deezer shows 231 fans, but TikTok virality of North Pole may mean higher Spotify monthlies; check. Thinnest sourcing of the five. Track naming is muddled (Shazam lists 'fat bx 3', Hipstrumentals 'Fat bx 1'). A Substack profile (genzmarquee 'Boohavinn is up next') exists but was not fetchable.

songs.title: If Not Soon Then Now
songs.verdict: A Brooklyn jangle-pop pair's first new song in two years puts bright melody over gritty guitars and pins down the worry that old baggage will wreck a new relationship.
songs.body:
Trinket are a Brooklyn indie rock and jangle pop band built around Madison Kate Proffitt and Sean Camargo, and both keep busy elsewhere: Proffitt also plays in Lightheaded and Betty Brite, while Camargo leads the post-punk band S.C.A.B. They released the New Hobby EP in 2024, have been a fixture on Brooklyn's live circuit, and have opened for the Pains of Being Pure at Heart and Heavenly, which tells you a lot about their lineage.

"If Not Soon Then Now" came out on 27 October 2026, their first new music since that EP and their first release after signing with the indie label Take Care Records. A debut album is planned for 2027. The band say the song is about starting a new relationship and realizing that your insecurities and leftover baggage from the last one come along for the ride, plus the fear that worrying about ruining a good thing could end up causing it.

Stereogum put it at the top of its weekly best songs list, hearing bright melody and synths over gritty guitars. It belongs in the indie pop and jangle tradition that runs from Heavenly through the Pains of Being Pure at Heart, and the band will support Starcleaner Reunion at their album release show.
songs.scout_note: Lane: Brooklyn jangle pop / indie rock, small indie label (Take Care Records). Listener count not verified, likely small. Also on LOBF New Music Discovery 30 Oct. Older Bandcamp seen in search: https://itstrinket.bandcamp.com/album/new-hobby (not the new song). songs.title: La Sombra
songs.verdict: A young Southeast London producer making the case that UK funky still has legs, three tracks of log drums, vocal chops and speed-garage bass.
songs.body:
sonny makepeace is a Southeast London producer, credited as Sonny Blue Makepeace, whose taste was shaped by growing up around sound system culture at festivals. That background shows up in a wide spread of influences, from progressive house and techno to grime, breaks and dubstep. Releases go back to the 2021 single "Eighteen," followed by the timeout EP in 2025 and a string of 2026 singles including "been here before," "somuch3basil" and the LOST bundle.

La Sombra arrived on October 16, 2026 via Funky Adjacent, framed by the label as the work of one of a new wave of young producers pushing UK funky forward. It has three tracks. "Fresh Soil," with SL KEN, was inspired by repotting a plant and leans on soulful chops and bouncy log drums. "Spida Plant," with Romaine, was written in a hard stretch and is about letting go, over jazzy chords and a bleepy bassline. "Mango Loco," with Naomi Nemi, mixes swung percussion with speed-garage bass, and the producer adds that they simply love mangoes. Joker is credited with mastering.

Bandcamp Daily heard French touch filter sweeps and Todd Edwards-style vocal cutting in the mix, sitting it in the current UK funky revival.
songs.scout_note: Lane: UK funky / UKG revival. Release date Oct 16, 2026, Funky Adjacent, tracklist, credits (produced by Sonny Blue Makepeace, mastered by Joker, words by Holly Barrett, vocals SL KEN/Romaine/Naomi Nemi), track stories, festival sound-system bio: https://sonnymakepeace.bandcamp.com/album/la-sombra and https://beatburguer.com/sonny-makepeace-la-sombra-funky-adjacent/ (Nov 9, 2026; mango line). Discography and Apple date: https://music.apple.com/ru/artist/sonny-makepeace/1522773000 (only a Russian-storefront Apple URL was seen; swap to /us/ if it resolves). French touch / Todd Edwards comparison: https://daily.bandcamp.com/best-electronic/the-best-electronic-music-on-bandcamp-october-2026. Bandcamp text gives IG as '@mapekeace' (possible typo, left artist_ig blank). Doubts: listener count unknown, almost certainly small. 'Joker' mastering credit not confirmed to be the Bristol producer, so don't overclaim. Body mentions Funky Adjacent as label per Bandcamp text.
